I added a `habit remind` command. It lists every habit you haven't marked done today, or says "All habits done for <date>" when there's nothing left. "Today" is the UTC date, like the rest of the app. `npm test` passes (9/9), including two new tests for `remind`. I couldn't run the real CLI by hand because the permission system blocked those shell commands; I didn't try to get around the blocks.

The change is in `src/commands.js`, `src/cli.js`, the README, and `test/commands.test.js`.

**Decision for you:** how reminders actually reach people. `remind` only prints a list, so something still has to run it. Options:
1. **Shell startup (my pick):** add `habit remind` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc` so it shows in every new terminal. It needs no code change, just a README note.
2. **Scheduled check:** run it from cron at a set time, e.g. 8pm. For that I'd add an exit code (non-zero when habits are pending) or a `--quiet` flag so it only prints when something is left.
3. **Desktop notifications:** pop up a system notification. This would depend on the OS (`notify-send` on Linux, `osascript` on macOS) and adds the most complexity.

Also note that because days are UTC, users far from UTC will see "today" roll over at an odd local time. It may be worth switching to local days later.
